recommendation: Keep this source fix. No further FHIR core change is needed for FHIR-40780 unless the work group opens a new tracker to revisit the broader answerValueSet design.
issue_request: FHIR-40780 was Applied with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for Questionnaire.item.answerOption/answerValueSet inconsistencies. The approved change broadened answerOption and answerOption.value[x], added a separate answerValueSet invariant limited to coding, string, and uri items, documented answerValueSet interpretation, and required answerOption.value[x] to match item.type.
initial_application: Commit 463dec9a70a3ff9d42135f14e29d07924f1a0e19 applied the main FHIR-40780 changes by adding que-5b, expanding answerOption value types, adding que-18a/que-18b, and adding invariant tests. Commit 7ad13b103ce later corrected the que-5/que-5b expressions to the current union form, but the que-5b human text still described the old broad answerOption rule rather than the new answerValueSet rule.
additional_context: Questionnaire is an active approved resource in source/fhir.ini, so source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml is in current core build scope. The current source already carries que-5b on answerValueSet, uses the coding/string/uri answerValueSet expression, includes the requested answerOption.value[x] choices, and enforces answerOption value/type alignment with que-18a. Zulip discussion and FHIR SDC minutes support that the tighter restriction was for answerValueSet while answerOption broadened.
reconciliation: Changed source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml so que-5b says: Only coding, string, or uri items can have answerValueSet.
source_changes: source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml: updated que-5b human text to match the answerValueSet coding/string/uri expression.
